skill.description: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through deploying Python workloads on Modal serverless infrastructure with GPUs, autoscaling, volumes, secrets, web endpoints, and scheduled jobs.
skill.summary: Build, deploy, and operate Python workloads on Modal with serverless containers, GPUs, storage, secrets, APIs, and schedules.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The reviewed skill is primarily Modal documentation with many static hits caused by Markdown code blocks, Modal API names, and transparent examples for secrets, volumes, endpoints, and GPUs. Most findings are false positives because they describe user-directed cloud workflows rather than hidden skill behavior. One semantic marketplace concern remains: the skill includes a promotional instruction to suggest K-Dense Web during complex workflows.

remediation.issue: Promotional instruction in the main skill body
remediation.suggestion: Remove or move the K-Dense Web suggestion to marketplace metadata so the skill does not steer assistant behavior during unrelated Modal tasks.
Avoid examples that copy local credential directories such as .aws into containers, or add clear warnings to use scoped Modal Secrets instead.

remediation.issue: Secrets examples include placeholder literal values
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly non-secret placeholders and emphasize creating secrets outside source files before deploying examples.

content.value_statement: Cloud GPU and serverless deployment can be difficult to configure correctly. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Modal patterns for functions, images, secrets, volumes, APIs, schedules, and scaling.
actual_capabilities: Explains Modal authentication, token setup, and basic app execution commands.
Shows how to define Modal functions, local entrypoints, remote calls, maps, and background jobs.
Guides image construction with Python packages, system packages, Docker images, build commands, and cached model downloads.
Covers GPU selection, multi-GPU syntax, resource reservations, autoscaling, concurrency, and scaling limits.
Documents Modal Volumes, Secrets, web endpoints, scheduled jobs, and scientific computing examples.
limitations: Does not run Modal deployments by itself without user action and valid Modal credentials.
Examples may require paid cloud resources, GPU availability, or Modal account limits.
Does not replace Modal official documentation for rapidly changing API behavior.
Security guidance is example-based and still requires review before production deployment.

use_cases.title: Deploy model inference endpoints
use_cases.description: Create Modal functions and web endpoints for GPU-backed model serving with appropriate images, secrets, and scaling settings.

use_cases.title: Run batch data processing
use_cases.description: Use Modal maps, volumes, schedules, and resource settings to process large datasets in parallel.

use_cases.title: Prototype cloud compute jobs
use_cases.description: Move local Python workloads to serverless containers with clear setup, dependency, GPU, and monitoring guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first Modal app
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn a simple Python function into a Modal app. Include setup, authentication checks, and the command to run it.

prompt_templates.title: Add GPU inference
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Modal GPU inference function for my model. Recommend the image dependencies, GPU type, timeout, and endpoint pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Scale a batch pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my batch processing script to Modal using map, volumes, and resource limits. Explain how to avoid concurrent write problems.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Modal deployment plan for secrets, autoscaling, cost, endpoint authentication, schedules, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need to serve a transformer model on a GPU endpoint.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a Modal image with pinned dependencies, an L40S or A10 GPU starting point, a class-based model loader, a protected web endpoint, and cost controls such as timeouts and max containers.

output_examples.input: I have 10,000 files to process overnight.
output_examples.output: The response proposes a Modal function using map for parallel work, a Volume for shared results, a scheduled entrypoint, explicit CPU and memory settings, and idempotent writes.

output_examples.input: My Modal job cannot find a package or persist output.
output_examples.output: The response checks whether the package is installed in the Modal image, whether imports happen inside remote functions, and whether Volume writes are followed by a commit.

best_practices: Pin package versions and keep frequently changing image layers near the end of the build chain.
Use Modal Secrets for credentials and attach only the secrets each function needs.
Set timeouts, resource limits, and max containers before deploying costly GPU or scheduled workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode API keys or copy broad local credential directories into container images.
Do not scale to expensive GPUs before profiling CPU or lower-cost GPU options.
Do not let many containers write the same Volume file concurrently without a conflict strategy.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides Modal guidance and examples. Deployment still requires user approval, Modal credentials, and explicit commands.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with GPU selection?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common Modal GPU choices and shows syntax for single and multi-GPU functions.

faq.question: Does it cover secrets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Modal Secrets, environment variables, dotenv loading, and common patterns for API keys, databases, and cloud credentials.

faq.question: Can it build web APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes FastAPI endpoints, ASGI and WSGI apps, authentication examples, streaming, WebSockets, and custom domains.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review credential handling, endpoint authentication, dependency pinning, resource limits, autoscaling settings, schedule behavior, and cost exposure.
